round_scores.evidence: Agent B: "Yeah, it's pretty strong... My room is right next to the kitchen..." Agent C: "My laundry, too. It's hanging right there." (Supports Agent A's initial request; establishes a substantive incompatibility between D's cooking and others' living conditions.)

Agent D: "That's the food I eat. It's what I grew up with." vs Agent A: "...the smell is still there when I'm on video calls with clients. It's not professional." (Directly conflicting interests/needs are stated.)

Agent B proposes a ventilation workaround: "Could we try opening the kitchen window? And maybe use a fan..." Agent C objects: "But my laundry is in the service yard. That would blow the smell straight into the clothes." (Introduces a proposed remedy and a new incompatibility.)

Agent B refines the solution: "What if we point the fan out the kitchen window instead?" Agent C: "Okay, that might work." (Some movement toward a compromise on ventilation, though not addressing all impacts or D's acceptance.)

Agent D: "The smell is very strong. I'm not sure how much a fan will help." Agent A: "She's right. I don't think a fan will be enough. That smell sticks around for hours." (Pushback on proposed remedy; disagreement about effectiveness.)

Agent B: "It might not be perfect, but it's better than nothing. We could at least try it." Agent C: "Yeah, we won't know unless we try." (Support for trial of ventilation, but effectiveness and other impacts still contested.)

Agent D: "So I set up a fan every time I cook? And if you still don't like the smell, then what? I just can't cook my food anymore?" Agent A: "...Could you cook it on weekends, or after 7 p.m. on weekdays?" (Stronger clash: D resists constraints on her cooking; A proposes scheduling limits.)

Agent D concedes: "Okay. After 7 on weekdays, or weekends. I can do that." Agent A: "Okay, great. Thanks." (Concrete agreement between A and D on cooking times, reducing that part of the conflict; other impacts not yet resolved.)

Agent B: "That helps with the living room, but it doesn't stop the smell from getting into my room and the laundry." Agent C: "Yeah, exactly. My laundry is still out there in the evenings." (New/remaining substantive issue: timing does not solve infiltration into private spaces and laundry.)

Agent B: "So what about the fan idea, then? Pointing it out the window when she's cooking?" Agent C: "Yeah, I still think we should try that." (Discussion returns to ventilation as a solution; D has not responded and concerns remain.)
